title: IPv6 Transition: The Complete Beginner's Guide

scenes.narration: Picture an office where some speak English, and others speak Spanish. The building has to work for everyone. It has three strategies.

scenes.heading: The bilingual building
scenes.narration: The manager has three approaches. Dual stack means everyone speaks both languages at once. A tunnel carries one language inside the other. A translator converts between the two. Dual stack is the preferred way, since nothing is translated.

scenes.heading: Tunnels
scenes.narration: Two tunnel types come up often. Six to four links sites over the internet, while I S A T A P works inside one site. Six to four uses the prefix two thousand two. Both are older methods.

rows.label: Used for
rows.l: Site to site over the internet

scenes.heading: Common mix-ups
scenes.narration: Three traps. Dual stack doesn't translate anything. Six to four and I S A T A P are different. N A T P T is deprecated, and N A T sixty four replaced it.

scenes.heading: Remember this
scenes.cta: Try the Courseiva IPv6 transition lab
scenes.narration: So, to recap. Dual stack runs both versions side by side. Tunnels carry I P six over I P four. N A T sixty four translates between them. Ready to practise? Try the Courseiva IPv6 transition lab.

points.t: Dual stack: both side by side
